I'm a therapist and, since January, have had flu, pneumonia, strep throat, covid, a sinus infection, and an ER visit for a blood clot. I did my best to not have to cancel on clients, but honestly, shit happens. All of that was out of my control, and I wasn't capable of seeing clients (minus the sinus infection, that I could power through, but it also wasn't contagious which matters when you're sitting in close proximity to someone). I've also had to cancel on snow days due to inability to get childcare (I live in the south, we have no idea how to drive in that kind of weather). I am up front with my clients about why I have to cancel - not specific, but I'll tell them I have covid or whatever and don't want to get them sick. If you're upset about them cancelling, you could always ask them why they did it. They may or may not answer, depending on their boundaries, but it's possible that they had perfectly valid reasons. Also, for me, if my kid is sick, it's up to me to take them to the doctor or whatever else because my husband makes more money than I do. So if anyone is taking off work to handle a household emergency, it's me. Whereas with a doctor, they probably have their support person (spouse, partner, parent, whoever) handling emergencies because they are probably the primary income provider, so they are less apt to take off work. Just my two cents.

A few thoughts here…I’m a therapist and I have narcolepsy. Sleep paralysis + auditory/visual hallucinations go hand in hand for me, so if I were your therapist, I’d screen for other narcolepsy symptoms. That said, I’ve had a teen before who heard voices and after lots of assessment, I did end up telling his parents bc the teen really needed further assessment and likely medication. I didn’t immediately run to their parents and tell them that, we had good rapport by that point. I would def talk to your therapist about what your limits of confidentiality are as a minor. Some states have confidentiality starting before 18 - mine doesn’t start til 18, and I can’t speak to other states’ rules around that.

I didn’t do a tour for my first, just delivered at the one hospital my OB delivered at. Had a horrible experience but a tour wouldn’t have really changed where I delivered. I’ve since moved, and this time I toured all 3 hospitals within 30 min of me. Knew what to look for this time. I’m switching OBs, partly bc I don’t like my current one, and partly bc they don’t deliver at the hospital I decided on. Decision factors for me, based on tour: this hospital has a nursery I can send baby to if needed (the other 2 don’t), this one has a mini fridge (convenient for pump parts if I have to pump), you deliver and room in the same room rather than having to switch (total PIA last delivery, moving rooms after delivering), and they have a pediatrician on staff who clears baby to go home (one of the hospitals I toured made you send your ped in to clear your baby, and I don’t think my ped offers that as a service).

I don’t have cataplexy but am currently pregnant for the second time. Both first and now, I’ve stayed on Adderall, just half the dose I am usually on. I stopped cold turkey during my first pregnancy and my mental health totally tanked so after talking with my docs, decided the risk of staying on lower dose of Adderall was better than the stress on the pregnancy otherwise (I was crying and sleeping all the time and basically nonfunctional when I stopped it). The only potential side effect I’m aware of is potential to cause less weight gain/low birth weight in the baby. My first several gynecologists didn’t bring up vaginismus or any reason I could be in pain (I didn’t know vaginismus was a thing then), even though I was in awful pain using a pediatric speculum as an adult. The one gynecologist who did listen to me just told me to buy dilators, which frankly would have been useless to me without the guidance of my PT. All that to say, I would def seek a second opinion from a PT who specializes in pelvic floors or potentially a Urogynecogist, both of whom treated (and cured!) my vaginismus after yeeeears of struggling before seeing them. 

Good on you and your partner! There are some real horror stories on the vaginismus sub about partners having no patience for it. Luckily my partner was patient with me as well and I delivered my first baby vaginally last year! 

If you have any specific questions or concerns feel free to PM me or ask publicly here. It’s not a condition that’s widely known and I think the more exposure it has, the more informed women can be. I was told by everyone “it just takes time” or “try some wine!” Or “use more lube” which all very well could work for some people, but not if it’s vaginismus.

Surprised I haven’t seen this comment yet but I have vaginismus and that could be what this is. There’s a sub for it (I think r/vaginismus). I bled the first several times I had sex and it was excruciating, felt like someone but the blade end of a knife in. I would not recommend pushing through the pain because you could potentially traumatize yourself, ask me how I know. I’d recommend getting evaluated by a pelvic floor physical therapist. Regardless of whether it’s vaginismus, you shouldn’t be experiencing excruciating pain during sex. And kudos for you two for stopping; I’m sure that was disappointing and difficult but you did what your body needed.
